OWL: Asks who, and hunts in the dark
JAY: Noisy, blue-flashed cousin of the crow
CROW: Black, clever, and gathers in a murder
DOVE: White bird that stands for peace
SWAN: Glides on the lake, mates for life
HAWK: Sharp-eyed hunter that hovers, then drops
WREN: Britain's tiniest bird, with a huge voice
LARK: Sings at dawn, and lends its name to early risers
IBIS: Curved beak, waded through ancient Egypt
KIWI: Flightless New Zealander with a long beak
ROBIN: Red breast on every Christmas card
EAGLE: King of the sky, and a golf score of two under
HERON: Stands motionless in the shallows, then strikes
CRANE: Long-legged dancer that shares its name with a lifting machine
RAVEN: Guards the Tower, and quoth nevermore
FINCH: Small seed-eater that gave Darwin his idea
GOOSE: Honks in a V, and lays a golden egg
QUAIL: Small game bird with tiny speckled eggs
MAGPIE: Black-and-white thief with an eye for shiny things
PIGEON: City bird that once carried the post
TOUCAN: Enormous colourful beak, at home in the rainforest

PARROT: Talks back, and rides a pirate's shoulder

PELICAN: Carries its catch in a great throat pouch
